transcript.content:
A user has filed a support ticket reporting that their experience
with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`
Available files: abnormal_metrics.parquet, abnormal_traces.parquet,
abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,
abnormal_metrics_sum.parquet, normal_metrics.parquet,
normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

content.text: I'll start by listing the tables and their schemas.
Next I'll compare per-service span counts, error rates and latency between the normal and abnormal periods.

input.query: SELECT 'normal' p, service_name, attr_span_kind, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) avg_ms, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,2) p95_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'abnormal', service_name, attr_span_kind, count(*), round(avg(duration)/1e6,2), round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,2), sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: The span volumes shifted a lot: `rate` and `reservation` nearly vanished in the abnormal period, and `search` and `profile` changed too. Next I'll break this down by span name and pod.

input.query: SELECT 'normal' p, service_name, span_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, attr_span_kind k, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) avg_ms, max(attr_status_code) st, max(attr_http_response_status_code) code FROM normal_traces GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'abnormal', service_name, span_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, attr_span_kind, count(*), round(avg(duration)/1e6,2), max(attr_status_code), max(attr_http_response_status_code) FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: I have enough to answer. Only the `/hotels` path failed, and it traces back to geo's crash loop.

input.reflection: Findings: geo pod crash-looping (restarts 0->6, ready=0, no container CPU/mem metrics, zero geo server spans abnormal vs 1161 normal). search's geo.Geo/Nearby client spans collapse to 0.02ms and search logs "Failed to get nearby hotels from geo service" (1533 errors). frontend /hotels returns 500 on 1103 requests (normal: all 200). Downstream rate/reservation/profile volume collapses only because search fails before calling them; they are not independent faults. No hubble network metrics; no other restarts. So one root cause: geo, pod-level (pod_unavailable class). Propagation: geo -> search -> frontend.

So one root cause: geo, pod-level (pod_unavailable class). Propagation: geo -> search -> frontend.
